properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. The reflow2 half of @ajs's brainstorm of 2026-09-29. The whole question lives in flo2's design (graph 1a97fc1f1de4d5d2) as dec:idea-should-flo2-manage-the-many-agent-sessions-working-its-designs.

In his words there: "we have a much more distributed set of agents and human users, but there might be some ideas of how flo2 (and maybe even reflow2) can manage this distributed asynchronous set of agents/users all working from overlapping sets of reflow2 designs."

WHERE IT COMES FROM: two multi-agent managers reviewed that day.
- orca (github.com/stablyai/orca at d0db35c).
- paseo (github.com/getpaseo/paseo at 264f6e1).
Both isolate agents by giving each its own copy of the code, and neither coordinates agents over SHARED state. reflow2's advisory claims already go further than either. What they have that reflow2's claims lack is the SUPERVISION layer: what a session is doing, and honesty about whether it is still alive.

TWO THINGS A CLAIM COULD CARRY, options none chosen:
(a) A STATE WITH A REASON. The states: working, waiting on a person (and the pending question itself), blocked, done. Plus a short checkpoint note, updated by the session and read before being overwritten.
  - orca: every agent is working / blocked / waiting / done, and the pending question rides with the state; agents keep a free-text checkpoint comment beside a phase status.
  - paseo: each agent carries an attention flag with a reason and a timestamp.
  - A claim already takes a `note` ("why it is held / what is being done"). This would add a closed state and let the note be REVISED during the claim, rather than set once at claim time.
  - It is what a flo2 dashboard's "Needs you" lane would read.
(b) LIVENESS HONESTY. Only the server that holds the session may say it has STOPPED. Every other reader, including after a restart, reports "unverifiable", never `gone`.
  - orca's rule is "no asserting what you cannot observe"; a status restored from disk is flagged unconfirmed and never reads as live.
  - This answers the measured defect in which two ACTIVELY working sessions' claims both read `gone` on the shared server (fact:two-active-sessions-claims-both-read-gone-2026-09-22), and the `unknown` a hosted design reports.
  - cap:claim-liveness already has the vocabulary: live / unknown / gone. The rule would narrow WHO may say `gone`.

COUNTERS, recorded beside them:
- For (a): a state the session must keep updating is only as true as the session's discipline. orca feeds its state from agent hooks, not from the agent's goodwill. A state that goes stale reads confident, which is the failure this design has counted twelve times in one session (fact:twelve-records-that-still-read-confident). A claim's state would need an age, and it should read "unverifiable" once too old.
- For (b): whether this is a new rule or simply the correct fix of the 2026-09-22 defect is itself open. That defect has not been root-caused.

SIZE, as information: (b) is small, and is really the defect fix. (a) is small to medium: a closed state on the claim, a revisable note, and claim_report / loop_status showing them.
properties.name: SETTLED — promoted into: A claim reads `gone` only when the server holding its session saw that session end; every other reader reports it unverifiable (and 1 more)
